common_name: Eastern woodland sedge / common wood sedge
look_here_first: Woodland Carex with relatively broad, flat green leaves and a loose set of separate spikes: one terminal staminate spike above several pistillate spikes.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays County is present in the repaired Master Plant Pool local-native source. Broader county reconciliation intentionally deferred under the provisional-first learning workflow.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for visual learning now; native metrics remain excluded until county-level review is completed.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Cyperaceae/Carex: grasslike perennial sedges with sheathing leaves; Carex fruits are enclosed in a perigynium, a key structure for species-level identification.
best_field_traits: flat leaves, often noticeably broader than cedar sedge
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Compared with C. planostachys, C. blanda usually has broader flatter leaves and taller looser foliage. Compared with C. edwardsiana, it lacks the strongly purple-red culm bases and Central Texas canyon-endemic pattern.
